---
title: "Mixtures of frontier reports"
subtitle: "2.11 · after the postrank theory book, ch. 22 and 25"
description: "Randomization over complete reports at a specified mean disclosure."
---

Randomizing between two frontier corner reports achieves any intermediate mean number of stated pairs along $H(m)$, often with far fewer expected wrong directions than any single report at that disclosure.

```{=html}
<div id="app" class="prx-app column-page"></div>

<script src="../../js/vendor/plot.min.js"></script>
<script src="../../js/bundles/frontier-mixtures.js"></script>
<script>window.__prxApp = PRX["frontier-mixtures"].mountWidget(document.getElementById("app"));</script>
```

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Six sites, mean 10.** Mixing the 12-pair report (chance .50) and the 8-pair report yields .0171 expected wrong directions; no single report states this count.
- **Six sites, mean 9.** Giving the upper report chance .25 yields .0133 expected wrong directions versus .160 for the best single report, a gap of .146.
- **Six sites, mean 12.** At a frontier corner (.0248 expected wrong directions), no mixture is needed.
- **Four units, mean 4.** Mixing the two endpoint reports with chance 1/2 gives 19/40 expected weighted wrong directions against 7/10 for the best single report (gap 9/40).
- **At most 3 grades, mean 9.** The capped family of 603 reports ends at 12 stated pairs, so the half-cost endpoint is **not guaranteed for this family**.

<details>
<summary>Endpoint conditions and notes</summary>

The half-cost endpoint requires the full report family and no latent ties on positive-weight criteria. In the endpoint disclosure, the fixed-order example shows a different restriction whose boundary misses the full ranking at $\tau = 1/2$. The six sites and the finite laws use posteriors specified for the examples.

</details>

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="In postrank"}
```r
library(postrank)
g <- list(c(A=1,B=1,C=2,D=2,E=2,F=2), c(A=1,B=1,C=2,D=2,E=3,F=3))
vapply(g, function(x) postrank_evaluate(x, pr_tutorial$one, weights=c(score_A=1), tau=.20)$E[1], numeric(1))
```

This evaluates the two complete reports at the mixture's endpoints. Their error counts appear in the vertex table. The average point weights those counts by the two selection probabilities.
:::
